subject: maths
question: An article is sold at a discount of 12.5%, and still there is a profit of 15%. At what approximate percentage over and above its cost price has the mark-up price of the article been fixed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%) = (100 − 12.5) : (100 + 15) = 87.5 : 115

Mark-up amount = 115 − 87.5 = 27.5

Mark-up % = (27.5 ÷ 87.5) × 100 = (11 ÷ 35) × 100 ≈ 31.43%

**∴ The correct answer is 31.43%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount (D) = 12.5%

Profit (P) = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + P ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D ÷ 100)
